corpus_definition: feeling bored or annoyed by something you have done too much
usage_note: be/get tired of + noun or -ing: "I am tired of waiting." Different from "tired from" = needing rest after doing something.

relations.note: Informal: bored and annoyed, very common in British English.
Not interested any more; less annoyed.
Liking something and wanting to do it.

context.text: Bobur is tired of eating plov every day. His sister is also getting tired of it, so tonight they are cooking soup.

reviewer_note: Not a phrasal verb (adjective + preposition), so kind phrase; tired from noted as a trap.

corpus_definition: a small object used to help perform a manual task.

forms.definition: an object you hold in your hand to help you do a job
forms.example: A hammer is a useful tool.

syn.note: A tool for careful or exact work, like in medicine or science.
A machine or object made for one job, often electric.
All the things you need for a job; uncountable.

forms.note: "tool up" exists only in rare informal use.

context.text: My grandfather keeps every tool in an old wooden box. When something breaks at home, he always has the right tool.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows with the same meaning merged. toolbox/toolkit are compounds, left out (rule 7).

corpus_definition: A hard white object in the mouth used for chewing food.

forms.definition: one of the hard white things in your mouth that you bite with
forms.example: The dentist looked at my bad tooth.

syn.note: A long sharp tooth of an animal like a dog or snake.

forms.example: The baby gave us a toothless smile.

context.text: My little brother lost his first tooth yesterday. Now he has a funny toothless smile in every photo.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: example says "brush my tooth"; normally "brush my teeth". toothbrush, toothpaste, toothache are compounds, left out (rule 7).

corpus_definition: a small mark or sign left by someone or something

forms.definition: a small sign or mark that shows someone or something was there
forms.example: There was no trace of the lost cat.

syn.note: Something that shows that something exists or happened.
A small spot or line on a surface.
Facts or things that show something is true; more formal.

forms.definition: to find someone or something by following signs they left
forms.example: The police traced the phone to a house in Chilonzor.
forms.note: Also "trace a picture" = copy it through thin paper.

syn.note: Follow the marks or signs of something.
General word; trace means finding step by step.
Find the exact place; more formal.

ant.note: Not know any more where someone or something is.

forms.definition: possible to find or follow back to where it came from

ant.note: Impossible to find or follow back.

context.text: Someone took Nodira's bag at the station, but there was no trace of the thief. Later the police traced him with the help of a camera.

reviewer_note: Verb trace (follow) is the same family; tracing a picture noted.

corpus_definition: All the cars and trucks on the road.

forms.definition: all the cars, buses and lorries moving on the roads
forms.example: There is heavy traffic in the city centre this morning.

syn.note: Too much traffic, so cars move slowly; more formal.
The cars and lorries themselves.

forms.definition: to buy and sell things like drugs or weapons illegally
forms.example: The men were caught trafficking drugs.
forms.note: Belongs to traffic = illegal trade, not cars on the road.

people.definition: a person who buys and sells drugs or weapons illegally
people.example: The police arrested a drug trafficker.
people.note: Belongs to traffic = illegal trade, not cars.

context.text: The traffic on Amir Temur Street was terrible today. Aziza was late for work because of the traffic.

reviewer_note: Verb and trafficker belong to the illegal-trade sense, so other_meaning. traffic jam/lights are compounds, left out.

corpus_definition: To change words from one language to another.

forms.definition: words that have been changed into another language, or the work of doing this
forms.example: I read the book in Uzbek translation.

syn.note: One form of a text, for example in another language.
Changing spoken words into another language.

forms.definition: to change spoken or written words into another language
forms.example: Can you translate this letter into English?

syn.note: Usually for spoken words, at the same time someone speaks.
"Put it into Russian" = say or write it in Russian.

forms.definition: possible to change into another language
forms.example: Some jokes are not easily translatable.

ant.note: Impossible to say well in another language.

people.definition: a person whose job is changing writing into another language
people.example: My aunt works as a translator in Tashkent.

context.text: Kamola translates English songs into Uzbek for fun. Her translation of one song became popular online.

reviewer_note: interpreter belongs to interpret, not this family.

corpus_definition: A person who is going on a journey to another place.

forms.definition: a person who is going on a journey
forms.example: The tired traveler needed a place to sleep.

syn.note: A person who travels for holiday and sightseeing.
A person travelling in a bus, train or plane who is not driving.

forms.definition: the activity of going from one place to another
forms.example: Air travel is faster than going by bus.

syn.note: The activity of going on journeys.
One trip from one place to another; countable.

forms.definition: to go from one place to another, often far away
forms.example: We travel to Khiva every summer.
forms.note: British English: travelled, travelling; American English: traveled, traveling.

syn.note: More formal or literary.
Travel to many places on a holiday.
General word.

context.text: Many travelers come to Samarkand in spring. They travel from all over the world to see the Registan.

reviewer_note: Headword is a person noun, so it stays the main noun entry (rule 6); travel is the base verb.

corpus_definition: A flat object used for carrying food or drinks.

forms.definition: a flat piece of wood, metal or plastic for carrying food and drinks
forms.example: She brought the tea on a tray.

syn.note: You eat from a plate; you carry things on a tray.
A large flat dish for serving food.

context.text: Grandma came into the room with a big tray. On it were bread, tea and a bowl of grapes.

corpus_definition: to put on clothing to see if it fits well.
particle_note: Separable: "try on the shoes / try the shoes on"; with a pronoun only "try them on".

relations.note: Put clothes on your body, but not to test them.
Be the right size: "Do the shoes fit?"

context.text: At the market, Dilshod tried on three jackets. He liked the brown one, so he tried it on again before he paid.

reviewer_note: Pronoun position (try it on) shown in context.

corpus_definition: a simple, pleasant series of musical notes; a melody

forms.definition: a series of musical notes that is nice to hear
forms.example: She hummed a happy tune while cooking.

syn.note: Same meaning; a little more formal.
Music with words; a tune can have no words.

forms.definition: to make a musical instrument play the right notes
forms.example: He tuned his dutar before the concert.
forms.note: "tune in" = choose a radio or TV station, a different use.

syn.note: Change something a little so it works better.

forms.definition: having a pleasant sound that is nice to listen to
forms.example: The children sang a tuneful song.

syn.note: Having a nice tune.

forms.definition: in a way that sounds pleasant and musical
forms.example: The birds sang tunefully in the garden.

people.definition: a person whose job is making pianos play the right notes
people.example: The piano tuner came on Monday.

context.text: My uncle tunes his dutar every evening. Then he plays an old tune that my grandmother loved.

reviewer_note: tuner is also a device in a radio; job sense kept.
